title: Share Trading Policy

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: All Directors and their spouses and any Related Party; the CEO, the Chief Operating Officers and the Chief Financial Officers of Group Companies; and all Key Management Personnel (as defined in AASB 124) not otherwise mentioned.

tiers.name: Chairman
tiers.description: The chairman of the Board; distinguished for the pre-dealing procedure (notifies the Company Secretary directly) and acts as the Designated Officer for other Restricted Persons' Excluded Dealing notices and exceptional-circumstances applications.

tiers.name: Director (other than the Chairman)
tiers.description: A director of the Company other than the Chairman; before dealing, must notify the Chairman (rather than the Company Secretary) of the intention to deal.

tiers.name: Restricted Persons (other than the Chairman or Directors)
tiers.description: Restricted Persons who are not the Chairman or a Director; before dealing, must notify the Company Secretary of the intention to deal.

definitions.hedging_definition: entering into a ... hedging arrangement which involves a Security holding in the Company

windows.start_anchor: release by the Company of half-yearly results to the ASX
release by the Company of preliminary final results to the ASX
any announcement by the Company to the ASX

rules.detail: Security has the meaning in the ASX Listing Rules and Dealing expressly extends to entering into a hedging arrangement involving a Security holding, with no venue limitation, so an OTC put/call is a Dealing requiring the clearance procedure in 3.2-3.3 and confined outside Closed Periods (or via an Excluded Dealing/exceptional-circumstances process within them).
rules.evidence: Deal or Dealing means buying or selling a Security holding in the Company or entering into a margin loan, scrip lending or hedging arrangement which involves a Security holding in the Company.

rules.detail: Hedging arrangements involving a Security holding are expressly named as a Dealing, with no separate prohibition and no vesting-based restriction (the Policy has no unvested/holding-lock concept). A hedge therefore requires the ordinary notify-and-clear procedure and must avoid Closed Periods, short-term-nature Dealing and possession of Inside Information.
rules.evidence: entering into a margin loan, scrip lending or hedging arrangement which involves a Security holding in the Company.

rules.detail: Monetisation structures such as a prepaid forward are not named; a sale or disposal of a Security holding, or a hedging arrangement, is a Dealing requiring the ordinary clearance procedure.
rules.evidence: Deal or Dealing means buying or selling a Security holding in the Company or entering into a margin loan, scrip lending or hedging arrangement which involves a Security holding in the Company.

rules.detail: Short selling is not named anywhere in the Policy or the Dealing definition.
Scrip lending is expressly named as a Dealing, requiring the same notify-and-clear procedure as any other Dealing, with no outright prohibition.
rules.evidence: entering into a margin loan, scrip lending or hedging arrangement which involves a Security holding in the Company.

rules.detail: CFDs are not named. A CFD over Austal shares functions as a hedging arrangement involving a Security holding, so it is a Dealing requiring the ordinary clearance procedure.
rules.evidence: entering into a margin loan, scrip lending or hedging arrangement which involves a Security holding in the Company.

rules.detail: Entering into a margin loan involving a Security holding is expressly a Dealing (clause 10) and also triggers clause 9's requirement of the Designated Officer's prior written consent before granting a lender rights over Company Securities. There is no outright prohibition.
rules.evidence: a Restricted Person must not enter into any Dealing or arrangement that provides lenders with rights over their interests in the Company's Securities without first obtaining the prior written consent of the Designated Officer.

rules.detail: Granting any lender rights over a Restricted Person's interest in Company Securities (a charge, pledge or similar) is expressly addressed and permitted only with the Designated Officer's prior written consent.
rules.evidence: a Restricted Person must not enter into any Dealing or arrangement that provides lenders with rights over their interests in the Company's Securities without first obtaining the prior written consent of the Designated Officer.

rules.detail: Clause 9 covers any Dealing or arrangement giving a lender rights over Company Securities, not just margin loans, so a bespoke bank loan secured on the collared shares is expressly captured and expressly permitted, subject only to the Designated Officer's prior written consent.
rules.evidence: Without limiting any other provision of this policy, a Restricted Person must not enter into any Dealing or arrangement that provides lenders with rights over their interests in the Company's Securities without first obtaining the prior written consent of the Designated Officer.

rules.detail: Dealing of a short-term nature is banned at all times, but 'short-term' is not defined by reference to a specific period (unlike a fixed 3- or 6-month rule), leaving the assessment to the Designated Officer/Chairman.
rules.evidence: a Restricted Person must not Deal in the Company's Securities: (a) where the Dealing is of a short-term nature

clearance.post_trade_deadline: within two Business Days of the Dealing
clearance.evidence: the Chairman must: (i) notify the Company Secretary of the Chairman's intention to Deal (or cause someone else to Deal) in the Company's Securities; (ii) confirm that the Chairman does not hold any Inside Information; and (iii) have been advised by the Company Secretary that there is no known reason to preclude the Chairman from Dealing in the Company's Securities as notified.

clearance.post_trade_deadline: within two Business Days of the Dealing
clearance.evidence: a Director (other than the Chairman) must: (i) notify the Chairman of the Director's intention to Deal (or cause someone else to Deal) in the Company's Securities; (ii) confirm that the Director does not hold any Inside Information; and (iii) have been advised by the Chairman that there is no known reason to preclude him/her from Dealing.

clearance.tier: Restricted Persons (other than the Chairman or Directors)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: within two Business Days of the Dealing
clearance.evidence: Restricted Persons (other than the Chairman or Directors) must: (i) notify the Company Secretary of their intention to Deal (or cause someone else to Deal) in the Company's Securities; (ii) confirm that they do not hold any Inside Information; and (iii) have been advised by the Company Secretary that there is no known reason to preclude them from Dealing.

clearance.approver: the Designated Officer (Chairman, or Company Secretary if the Restricted Person is the Chairman)
clearance.evidence: a Restricted Person must not enter into any Dealing or arrangement that provides lenders with rights over their interests in the Company's Securities without first obtaining the prior written consent of the Designated Officer.

short_term.evidence: a Restricted Person must not Deal in the Company's Securities: (a) where the Dealing is of a short-term nature

exceptions.evidence: he or she has a pressing financial commitment that cannot be satisfied otherwise than by selling or disposing of the relevant Securities of the Company.
a court order; a court enforceable undertaking; or some other overriding legal or regulatory requirement for the Restricted Person to do so, to be exceptional circumstances.

The Designated Officer may consider other circumstances to be exceptional circumstances for the purposes of paragraph 5(a), if the Designated Officer is satisfied that the proposed Dealing is the only reasonable course of action available to the Restricted Person.
transfers of the Company's Securities by the Restricted Person into a superannuation fund or other saving scheme in which the Restricted Person is a beneficiary

an investment in, or trading in units of, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme only investing in the Company's Securities) where the assets of the fund or other scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party

where a Restricted Person is a trustee, trading in the Company's Securities by that trust provided the Restricted Person is not a beneficiary of the trust and any decision to trade during a Closed Period is taken by the other trustees or by the investment managers independently of the Restricted Person
undertakings to accept, or the acceptance of, a takeover offer for the Company

accepting an offer or invitation made by the Company to all or most of its security holders, such as a rights issue, a security purchase plan, a dividend or distribution reinvestment plan and an equal access buy-back, where the plan that determines the timing and structure of the offer has been approved by the Board

a disposal of the Company's Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement (note the rules applicable to Restricted Persons entering into arrangements that provide lenders with rights over their interests in the Company's Securities in paragraph 9 of this policy)

the exercise (but not the sale of the Company's Securities following exercise) of an option or a right under an employee incentive scheme, or such similar scheme or plan, or the conversion of a convertible security, where the final date for the exercise of the option or right, or the conversion of the security, falls during a Closed Period

trading under a non-discretionary trading plan for which Prior Written Clearance has been provided in accordance with paragraph 5 and where: (i) the Restricted Person did not enter into the plan or amend the plan during a Closed Period; (ii) the trading plan does not permit the Restricted Person to exercise any influence or discretion over how, when, or whether to trade
a Dealing which results in no change in the beneficial interest in the Company's Securities.

financing_disclosure: Restricted Persons: trigger = inception (before entering into any Dealing or arrangement giving a lender rights over their interests in Company Securities); to whom = the Designated Officer; deadline = prior written consent must be obtained before entering into the arrangement (clause 9).

exemption_authority: The Designated Officer (the Chairman for all Restricted Persons other than the Chairman; the Company Secretary where the Chairman is the Applicant) may grant Prior Written Clearance to sell or otherwise dispose of Securities during a Closed Period for severe financial hardship or other exceptional circumstances (a court order, enforceable undertaking, other overriding legal or regulatory requirement, or any circumstance the Designated Officer is satisfied is the only reasonable course of action), responding within 14 days of a written Application lodged at least 21 days beforehand; approval may be conditioned in the Designated Officer's absolute discretion, and rejection (given without reasons) is final.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Without limiting any other provision of this policy, a Restricted Person must not enter into any Dealing or arrangement that provides lenders with rights over their interests in the Company's Securities without first obtaining the prior written consent of the Designated Officer.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is the operative gate for the funded collar's loan leg: granting the bank security over the collared shares is expressly permitted, but only with the Designated Officer's (the Chairman's, or the Company Secretary's if the executive is the Chairman) prior written consent -- there is no blanket ban on secured financing as seen in many peer policies.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging and scrip lending are express Dealings
bespoke_clauses.clause: Deal or Dealing means buying or selling a Security holding in the Company or entering into a margin loan, scrip lending or hedging arrangement which involves a Security holding in the Company.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar (a hedging arrangement) and a margin loan are both expressly named as Dealings, so the put/call legs and the loan leg both sit within the ordinary clearance and Closed Period framework rather than a separate prohibition.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a Restricted Person must not Deal in the Company's Securities: (a) where the Dealing is of a short-term nature
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike policies with a fixed 3- or 6-month rule, 'short-term nature' is undefined, leaving the Chairman/Designated Officer discretion to treat an early unwind or short-dated collar as prohibited; a longer-dated structure reduces this risk.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a disposal of the Company's Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement (note the rules applicable to Restricted Persons entering into arrangements that provide lenders with rights over their interests in the Company's Securities in paragraph 9 of this policy)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank's enforcement sale on default can proceed during a Closed Period as an Excluded Dealing, but only after a 7-business-day Excluded Dealing Notice to the Designated Officer, who can block it without giving reasons.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons are: (a) All Directors and their spouses and any Related Party; (b) The Chief Executive Officer, the Chief Operating Officers, the Chief Financial Officers of Group Companies; and (c) All Key Management Personnel ... not otherwise mentioned.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Policy has no unvested/vested-locked distinction and no equity-plan hedging carve-out, so the same clearance and Closed Period rules apply uniformly to any vested shareholding used to fund a collar.

summary: A funded collar over Austal shares is comparatively achievable: 'Dealing' is expressly defined to include entering into a margin loan, scrip lending or hedging arrangement, so the put/call legs and the loan leg are Dealings governed by the ordinary clearance regime rather than being separately banned. Outside Closed Periods (broadly, within four months of a half-yearly or preliminary final results release, minus the 24 hours after any ASX announcement), a Restricted Person need only notify the Chairman or Company Secretary in writing, confirm no Inside Information, and be advised there is no known reason to preclude the deal, then notify again within two business days after dealing. Critically for the loan leg, clause 9 requires the Designated Officer's (the Chairman's, or the Company Secretary's if the executive is the Chairman) prior written consent before granting a lender rights over the collared shares -- an express gate, not a prohibition. A lender's enforcement sale during a Closed Period is possible as an Excluded Dealing but needs a 7-business-day advance notice and the Designated Officer's non-objection, which can be refused without reasons. Overall verdict: workable subject to the Designated Officer's consent to the security interest and timing within an open window or an Excluded Dealing/exceptional-circumstances process, with the undefined 'short-term nature' prohibition counselling a longer-dated structure.
